The overarching question: what is the marginal value of information in emergency epidemic intelligence, and is SPI-M fit for purpose?

Each idea is an [issue in this repository](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues), where its question, approach, sources and discussion live.
Ideas are grouped by where they sit in the chain that turns surveillance data into policy decisions.
Within each issue, the evaluation lens is quality, value or trust.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  D[Data] --> P[Process]
  E[Expertise] --> P
  P --> S[Estimates]
  S --> C[Decisions]
```

## Data

What each surveillance stream measured, and what it was worth.

- [Evaluating the ONS COVID-19 Infection Survey](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/8): what the CIS told us that routine data could not, and what it was worth.
- [Triangulating data sources for hazard and vulnerability](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/9): how risk assessment should combine streams, and the cost per unit of accuracy of each.
- [Bias audit of UK routine surveillance data](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/10): the delays and biases in the data local analysts actually receive.

## Expertise

Who was in the room, how they were found, and what it cost them.

- [Citation networks as a map of UK outbreak modelling expertise](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/11): who counts as an outbreak modeller, and where the blind spots are against national risks.
- [Career trajectories of outbreak responders](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/12): who stays in the field after a response.
- [Institutional SOP for redeploying researchers to emergencies](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/13): how institutions release people into a response, and what they owe them.

## Process

How many models became one statement.

- [ONS excess deaths and SPI-M consensus as two modes of production](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/14): supply-driven and demand-driven estimation compared on quality, value and trust.
- [How consensus is made](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/15): SPI-M practice against SHELF and DELPHI, and what good facilitation would look like.
- [Model genealogy](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/16): how independent the models behind the consensus really were.
- [Comparative institutional design for modelling advice](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/17): one advisor or many; champion and challenger, or consensus.

## Estimates

Whether the numbers and the words were right.

- [Calibrating SPI-M consensus statements](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/18): how well the R and growth rate ranges, and the language around them, matched what happened. Worked up in [explore-r-gr](explore-r-gr.qmd).
- [Exercise Pegasus](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/19): the same evaluation applied to the 2025 exercise.

## Decisions

What the advice changed, and who answers for it.

- [Accountability for advisory numbers](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/20): whether advisory bodies should be held to the same account as official statistics. Background in [evaluation](evaluation.qmd).
- [Tracing advice to decisions](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/21): which decisions the estimates fed, at what thresholds, and what errors near them cost.
- [What the COVID-19 Inquiry says about modelling advice](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/22): not yet developed. See the [comment on the end of the Inquiry](inquiry-evaluation.qmd).

## History

- [A natural history of SPI-M](https://github.com/kathsherratt/spi-m-o/issues/23): how SPI-M came to work as it does, across successive outbreaks from FMD in 2001 to Exercise Pegasus in 2025. See the [potted history](history.qmd).
